about: How a model is labelled and filed, by the label table of core/crates/inku-pipeline/data/model_catalog.json (the author, 2026-10-13). Each case gives a model in the common format: `labels` lists its stored labels, the ones written in the catalog (legacy, subscription, not_supported, eol), which an installation corrects for its own key (subscription after its key's probe, eol when a refetched list no longer offers the model); `purposes` are those it is offered for, already without its `unsupported_purposes` except those an administrator chose against the measurement (2026-10-26), and an absent `purposes` means ["llm"]. Two labels are worked out from the model: no_response when no purpose it is offered for is one it answers (`purposes` without `unsupported_purposes` is empty; since 2026-10-26 it can be published, as not recommended), and unmeasured when it carries no measurement and every other label lets it be published. A measurement is any of recommendation_llm, recommendation_vision, recommendation_stage1, recommendation_stage2, recommendation_level, speed_class, speed_label, speed_llm_seconds, speed_vision_seconds, cost_usd_llm, cost_usd_vision, comment_ja, comment_en, unsupported_purposes. Expected: every label in the table's order, the fold (the label that comes last in the table, or null to stay in the list) and whether it can be published (every label allows it). The Server, the Web, macOS and Android check themselves against these cases.
